/-!
# The infinite positive Laplace measure underlying paired eta

Finite paired-eta roots were realized as zeros of finite positive Laplace
transforms. This module removes the truncation. It constructs one fixed
positive measure by restricting Lebesgue measure to the disjoint logarithmic
intervals

`(log (2n+1), log (2n+2)]`.

The complex exponential is proved genuinely integrable against this measure
throughout `Re s > 0`. Its integral is exactly the absolutely convergent sum
of the interval Laplace transforms, and multiplication by `s` recovers the
full paired eta core. Therefore every nontrivial zeta zero is an exact zero of
this single positive-measure Laplace transform. Its real and imaginary parts
give literal, absolutely convergent tilted cosine and sine cancellations.

This is an unconditional infinite arithmetic representation. It turns the
zero-location frontier into rigidity of one explicit positive measure; it
does not itself prove that rigidity.
-/

open Complex Filter MeasureTheory Metric Set Topology
open scoped Classical ENNReal Interval Topology

namespace RiemannGaussian

noncomputable section

/-- The `n`th logarithmic interval carrying the positive paired-eta measure. -/
def pairedEtaLogInterval (n : ℕ) : Set ℝ :=
  Ioc (Real.log (2 * n + 1)) (Real.log (2 * n + 2))

/-- The complete logarithmic support of the positive paired-eta measure. -/
def pairedEtaLogSupport : Set ℝ :=
  ⋃ n : ℕ, pairedEtaLogInterval n

/-- Lebesgue measure restricted to the complete paired-eta logarithmic
support. -/
def pairedEtaLogMeasure : Measure ℝ :=
  volume.restrict pairedEtaLogSupport

/-- Distinct paired-eta logarithmic intervals are disjoint. -/
theorem pairwise_disjoint_pairedEtaLogInterval :
    Pairwise (fun n m : ℕ ↦
      Disjoint (pairedEtaLogInterval n) (pairedEtaLogInterval m)) := by
  suffices hordered : ∀ {n m : ℕ}, n < m →
      Disjoint (pairedEtaLogInterval n) (pairedEtaLogInterval m) by
    intro n m hne
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with hnm | hmn
    · exact hordered hnm
    · exact (hordered hmn).symm
  intro n m hnm
  apply Set.disjoint_left.mpr
  intro t htn htm
  have harg : (2 : ℝ) * n + 2 < 2 * m + 1 := by
    exact_mod_cast (show 2 * n + 2 < 2 * m + 1 by omega)
  have hlog : Real.log (2 * n + 2) < Real.log (2 * m + 1) :=
    Real.log_lt_log (by positivity) harg
  exact (not_lt_of_ge htn.2) (hlog.trans htm.1)

/-- The complete paired-eta logarithmic support is measurable. -/
theorem measurableSet_pairedEtaLogSupport :
    MeasurableSet pairedEtaLogSupport := by
  unfold pairedEtaLogSupport pairedEtaLogInterval
  exact MeasurableSet.iUnion fun _ ↦ measurableSet_Ioc

/-- The restricted measure is exactly the countable sum of the interval
restrictions. -/
theorem pairedEtaLogMeasure_eq_sum_restrict :
    pairedEtaLogMeasure =
      Measure.sum fun n : ℕ ↦ volume.restrict (pairedEtaLogInterval n) := by
  unfold pairedEtaLogMeasure pairedEtaLogSupport
  exact Measure.restrict_iUnion
    pairwise_disjoint_pairedEtaLogInterval
    (fun _ ↦ by
      unfold pairedEtaLogInterval
      exact measurableSet_Ioc)

/-- The paired-eta logarithmic measure is dominated by Lebesgue measure. -/
theorem pairedEtaLogMeasure_le_volume :
    pairedEtaLogMeasure ≤ volume := by
  exact Measure.restrict_le_self

/-- The complete logarithmic support lies in positive time. -/
theorem pairedEtaLogSupport_subset_Ioi_zero :
    pairedEtaLogSupport ⊆ Ioi 0 := by
  intro t ht
  rw [pairedEtaLogSupport, mem_iUnion] at ht
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := ht
  have hlogNonneg : 0 ≤ Real.log (2 * n + 1) := by
    apply Real.log_nonneg
    norm_num
  exact hlogNonneg.trans_lt hn.1

/-- The entire first interval `(0, log 2]` belongs to the logarithmic
support. -/
theorem Ioc_zero_log_two_subset_pairedEtaLogSupport :
    Ioc 0 (Real.log 2) ⊆ pairedEtaLogSupport := by
  intro t ht
  rw [pairedEtaLogSupport, mem_iUnion]
  refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
  simpa [pairedEtaLogInterval] using ht

/-- One logarithmic interval Laplace transform. -/
def pairedEtaLaplaceInterval (s : ℂ) (n : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  ∫ t : ℝ in Real.log (2 * n + 1)..Real.log (2 * n + 2),
    Complex.exp (-s * t)

/-- The infinite positive-measure Laplace partition function underlying
paired eta. -/
def pairedEtaLaplacePartition (s : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑' n : ℕ, pairedEtaLaplaceInterval s n

/-- The logarithmic Laplace intervals are absolutely summable throughout the
positive half-plane. -/
theorem summable_pairedEtaLaplaceInterval
    {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < s.re) :
    Summable (pairedEtaLaplaceInterval s) := by
  have hs0 : s ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    subst s
    norm_num at hs
  have hsum := (summable_pairedEtaCoreSummand hs).div_const s
  apply hsum.congr
  intro n
  rw [pairedEtaCoreSummand_eq_mul_logLaplaceInterval]
  simp [pairedEtaLaplaceInterval, hs0]

/-!
# Greedy-bump laws for exponential-polynomial mode packets

Distinct complex frequencies, with arbitrary finite multiplicities, give a strictly positive
interval Gram matrix.  Its doubled-real form is therefore a template metric for arXiv:2609.03581.
The total complex mode multiplicity controls the universal bias and localization coefficients;
frequencies and interval endpoints control only the metric shape.
-/

open Matrix
open scoped ComplexOrder

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Certified exponential-polynomial packet on a nondegenerate real interval. -/
structure GreedyBumpExponentialModeData (r : ℕ) where
  frequency : Fin r → ℂ
  frequency_injective : Function.Injective frequency
  multiplicity : Fin r → ℕ
  left : ℝ
  right : ℝ
  interval_nonempty : left < right

/-- Total number of complex exponential-polynomial modes, including multiplicities. -/
def GreedyBumpExponentialModeData.modeCount {r : ℕ}
    (data : GreedyBumpExponentialModeData r) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i, data.multiplicity i

/-- Doubled-real interval Gram matrix of the exponential-polynomial packet. -/
def GreedyBumpExponentialModeData.realifiedMatrix {r : ℕ}
    (data : GreedyBumpExponentialModeData r) :
    Matrix (Fin (data.modeCount + data.modeCount))
      (Fin (data.modeCount + data.modeCount)) ℝ :=
  (GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.complexMatrixRealification
      (exponentialPolynomialIntervalGram data.frequency data.multiplicity
        data.left data.right)).submatrix finSumFinEquiv.symm finSumFinEquiv.symm

/-- Exponential-polynomial interval Gram as a positive template metric. -/
def GreedyBumpExponentialModeData.metric {r : ℕ}
    (data : GreedyBumpExponentialModeData r) :
    GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.PositiveTemplateMetric
      (data.modeCount + data.modeCount) where
  matrix := data.realifiedMatrix
  posDef := (GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.complexMatrixRealification_posDef
    (exponentialPolynomialIntervalGram_posDef data.frequency_injective
      data.multiplicity data.interval_nonempty)).submatrix finSumFinEquiv.symm.injective

/-- Complete optimizer, trials, bias, and localization laws for every certified mode packet. -/
theorem GreedyBumpExponentialModeData.laws {r : ℕ}
    (data : GreedyBumpExponentialModeData r)
    (Q : GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.PositiveSignal) :
    GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.GreedyBumpMetricLaws Q data.metric :=
  GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.greedyBumpMetricLaws_closed Q data.metric

/-- A packet of `M` complex modes has leading amplitude bias `M / Q`. -/
theorem GreedyBumpExponentialModeData.bias {r : ℕ}
    (data : GreedyBumpExponentialModeData r)

/-!
# Compact proper-time convergence

This file upgrades the complete fixed-positive-time polynomial heat limit to
convergence of heat actions on every compact proper-time interval bounded away
from zero.

The key point is intrinsic to the hyperbolic heat kernel.  At positive proper
time it is an integral of `exp (-x * t)` over the interval between the two
squared hyperbolic distances.  Those endpoints are nonnegative and ordered
for two upper-half-plane points, so every one-root heat term, every finite
upper divisor heat, and hence every polynomial upper heat is antitone in
proper time.  Pointwise convergence at the left endpoint of `[a, b]` therefore
gives one stage-independent constant dominating the entire sequence on that
interval.  Lebesgue dominated convergence then identifies the limiting
compact heat action with the interval integral of the complete spectral-xi
heat sum.

Thus a Hardy defect cannot disappear in the interior of proper time.  Any
remaining failure to pass its positive total mass to the spectral limit must
escape through `t -> 0` or `t -> infinity`; controlling those two endpoints is
the next frontier.
-/

open Complex Filter MeasureTheory Metric Polynomial Set Topology
open scoped Classical Interval Topology

/-! ## Antitonicity of the positive-time heat kernel -/

/-- A divided difference of two real exponentials is an interval integral.
The positivity of `t` is used only to cancel the antiderivative's factor
`t⁻¹`. -/
theorem expDifferenceDiv_eq_intervalIntegral
    {A B t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    t⁻¹ * (Real.exp (-(A * t)) - Real.exp (-(B * t))) =
      ∫ x in A..B, Real.exp (-(x * t)) := by
  have hderiv (x : ℝ) :
      HasDerivAt
        (fun y : ℝ ↦
          -t⁻¹ * (Real.exp ∘ (-(fun u : ℝ ↦ id u * t))) y)
        (Real.exp (-(x * t))) x := by
    have hinner :
        HasDerivAt (-(fun y : ℝ ↦ id y * t)) (-(1 * t)) x :=
      ((hasDerivAt_id x).mul_const t).neg
    have hexp :=
      (Real.hasDerivAt_exp ((-(fun u : ℝ ↦ id u * t)) x)).comp x hinner
    have hscaled := hexp.const_mul (-t⁻¹)
    apply hscaled.congr_deriv
    simp only [Pi.neg_apply, id_eq, one_mul]
    field_simp [ne_of_gt ht]
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt
    (fun x _ ↦ hderiv x)
    ((by fun_prop : Continuous fun x : ℝ ↦
      Real.exp (-(x * t))).intervalIntegrable A B)]
  field_simp
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, Pi.neg_apply, id_eq]
  ring

/-- If `0 ≤ A ≤ B`, the exponential divided difference is antitone in
positive proper time. -/
theorem expDifferenceDiv_le_of_time_le
    {A B s t : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hAB : A ≤ B)
    (hs : 0 < s) (hst : s ≤ t) :
    t⁻¹ * (Real.exp (-(A * t)) - Real.exp (-(B * t))) ≤
      s⁻¹ * (Real.exp (-(A * s)) - Real.exp (-(B * s))) := by
  have ht : 0 < t := hs.trans_le hst
  rw [expDifferenceDiv_eq_intervalIntegral ht,
    expDifferenceDiv_eq_intervalIntegral hs]
  apply intervalIntegral.integral_mono_on hAB
  · exact (by fun_prop : Continuous fun x : ℝ ↦
      Real.exp (-(x * t))).intervalIntegrable A B
  · exact (by fun_prop : Continuous fun x : ℝ ↦
      Real.exp (-(x * s))).intervalIntegrable A B
  · intro x hx
    apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
    have hx0 : 0 ≤ x := hA.trans hx.1
    nlinarith

/-- For positive heights, one real-coordinate hyperbolic heat term is
antitone on positive proper time. -/
theorem pairHyperbolicHeatIntegrand_le_of_time_le
    {d v a s t : ℝ} (hv : 0 < v) (ha : 0 < a)
    (hs : 0 < s) (hst : s ≤ t) :
    pairHyperbolicHeatIntegrand d v a t ≤
      pairHyperbolicHeatIntegrand d v a s := by
  unfold pairHyperbolicHeatIntegrand
  exact expDifferenceDiv_le_of_time_le
    (pairHyperbolicUpperSq_nonneg d v a)
    (pairHyperbolicUpperSq_lt_lowerSq ha hv).le hs hst

/-- For two upper-half-plane points, one complex hyperbolic heat term is
antitone on positive proper time. -/
theorem upperHalfPlaneHyperbolicHeatIntegrand_le_of_time_le
    {z alpha : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) (halpha : 0 < alpha.im)
    {s t : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hst : s ≤ t) :
    upperHalfPlaneHyperbolicHeatIntegrand z alpha t ≤
      upperHalfPlaneHyperbolicHeatIntegrand z alpha s := by
  rw [upperHalfPlaneHyperbolicHeatIntegrand_eq_pair,
    upperHalfPlaneHyperbolicHeatIntegrand_eq_pair]
  exact pairHyperbolicHeatIntegrand_le_of_time_le hz halpha hs hst

/-- Every finite multiplicity-counted upper heat sum is antitone on positive
proper time. -/
theorem finiteUpperHyperbolicHeatSum_le_of_time_le
    {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) {upper : Multiset ℂ}
    (halpha : ∀ alpha ∈ upper, 0 < alpha.im)
    {s t : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hst : s ≤ t) :
    finiteUpperHyperbolicHeatSum z upper t ≤
      finiteUpperHyperbolicHeatSum z upper s := by
  induction upper using Multiset.induction_on with
  | empty => simp [finiteUpperHyperbolicHeatSum]
  | @cons alpha upper ih =>

# PW-B complete signed adjoint response passage

- **ID:** PW-B-GAMMA-ADJOINT-PAIRED-RESPONSE-2026-09-11
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Status:** Nineteen public theorems passed the final foreground Lean scratch without diagnostics. Exact source promoted and wired once; targeted leaf build passed in125s. All nineteen public names are indexed, and repository formal lint passed.
- **Scope:** Absolute joint admission of the complete signed backward response, original moving-cutoff mismatch limit and simultaneous native cutoff passage. Finite-cutoff gain transposition, full common-domain adjoints, Xi occurrence and independent Ward balance remain open. RH is not proved.
- **Depends on:** [complete reciprocal source bounds](pw-b-gamma-reciprocal-cutoff-source.md), [complete paired contact](pw-b-gamma-adjoint-paired-contact.md).

## Exact original-source statements

Retain the whole arithmetic source, with

`g_z(x)=M_z(x)/Q(x)`, `w(x)=exp(-x-1/x)/x`,

`S_z(t)=g_z(1/t)-1`,

`H_z(v,h)=exp(-h)*(S_z(v+h)-S_z(v))/h`,

`J_z,v(x,h)=w(x)*g_v(x)*conj(H_z(1/x,h))`.

For every two complex parameters z,v there are an integer r and a finite
C>=0 such that, for all positive x,h,

`|J_z,v(x,h)| <= C*x*exp(-x)*exp(-h)*(1+h)^r`.

Consequently J is absolutely integrable on the product of the two positive
rays. Every positive-x section is also absolutely integrable, not merely
almost every section.

For `a_delta(x)=delta/[x*(x-delta)]` on x>delta,

`integral_(x>delta) w(x)*g_v(x)*conj(integral_(a_delta(x)..delta) H_z(1/x,h) dh) dx -> 0`.

Both native cutoffs pass simultaneously:

`integral_(x>delta) w(x)*g_v(x)*conj(integral_(h>delta) H_z(1/x,h) dh) dx`

`-> integral_(x>0) w(x)*g_v(x)*conj(integral_(h>0) H_z(1/x,h) dh) dx`.

Limits are as delta tends to0 from above. Outer integrals in both cutoff
expressions and in the final response are admitted. The entire moving
mismatch layer and the originally omitted initial region remain in the
proof. The constant-field contact and its empty incoming constant loss
are retained separately in the previous paired-contact theorem.

## Proof

The source polynomial bound gives
`|g_v(x)|<=(1+A)*(1+1/x)^p`. The complete response estimate gives
`|H_z(1/x,h)|<=K*exp(-h)*(1/x+h)^r`.
Use

`(1/x+h)^r<=(1+1/x)^r*(1+h)^r`.

The elementary power bound and the original exponential factorial inequality

`w(x)/x^k<=(k+2)!*x*exp(-x)`

then absorb every inverse power in x. Gamma moments admit both factors
of the resulting product majorant. Global source measurability follows
from the actual atom sum; no pointwise numerical approximation is used.

Represent the two cutoff responses on one fixed positive product measure:

`J(x,h)*1_(x>delta,h>a_delta(x))`,

`J(x,h)*1_(x>delta,h>delta)`.

Each has norm at most |J|. For fixed positive x,h, both indicators are
eventually one, because a_delta(x) and delta tend to0. Dominated convergence
therefore takes both full product integrals to the integral of J.

Absolute admission justifies Fubini for each mask. The exact indicator
identities recover the original iterated integrals on x>delta. On every
such x, the difference of admitted tails is exactly the oriented interval
integral from a_delta(x) to delta. Subtracting the two limits proves the
mismatch theorem. Constants and complex conjugation commute with the actual
integrals, yielding the displayed original-source formulas.

## Remaining hard obstacle

This passage does not prove that the forward gain equals the transported
backward gain. That identity must still retain the triangle produced by
y=x+h and the reciprocal substitution r=1/(y-h)-1/y, with the original
Jacobian, full source and admitted integrals. After that identity, the
proved response limits and retained logarithmic contact can determine the
full paired adjoint defect. A physical operator domain, source-forced
geometry, a different justified Xi realization and independent Ward balance
remain additional requirements.

The precise corrected Gamma scalar ansatz is already excluded by the
[original-current valuation](../5-failed/pw-b-corrected-gamma-scalar-occurrence.md).
Neither the response admission nor a positive abstract dilation reverses
that obstruction.

## Exact source statements

Let S be any finite set of primes. Index the retained field by all subsets R

define

`V_S(M)(R)=sum_(1<=d<=M, primeFactors(d) intersect S=R) C_d(M)`.

For real coordinates y(R), its pairing is exactly

`<y,V_S(M)>=sum_(1<=d<=M) y(primeFactors(d) intersect S)*C_d(M)`.

All cutoffs are integers and all source channels, including their clipped

1. If `<y,V_S(M)> >= 0` for every M, then every coordinate y(R) is zero.
2. Every nonzero y has actual cutoffs with strictly positive and strictly

4. There also exist such K, c>0 and `0<delta<=1` for which every independent
   choice `0<=clip(M)<=delta`, M in K, satisfies: for every y, some M in K has

# CCM-FU: exact retained-source recursion and orientation reversal

- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** unconditional source homothety, mixed energy identity and cofinal orientation reversal
- **Source:** [adaptive original-diagonal ceiling PE4](../1-in-progress/ccm-fu-adaptive-prime-ceiling.md)
- **Boundary:** PE4, PE4G, SD1 and RH remain open. The recursion identifies the signed arithmetic comparison; it does not prove its required bound.

## Full retained-fibre copy

Write `F_(M,P)(R)` for the literal source retained at cofactor label R after processing P. For a prime p>N with p unprocessed, every source label divisible by p at cutoff pN is uniquely p*d with d<=N. The cofactor is coprime to p. Exact channel homothety and prime-factor bookkeeping give, whenever p is absent from R,

`F_(pN,P)(R union {p})=-sqrt(p)*F_(N,P)(R)`.

This is a copy of the entire retained source, with its original arithmetic weights. It includes zero and terminal coefficients and uses no asymptotic replacement. Processing p therefore gives

`F_(pN,P union {p})(R)=F_(pN,P)(R)-sqrt(p)*F_(N,P)(R)`

for every p-free retained label R; all labels still containing p disappear. The head is the case R empty.

## Exact mixed energy update

For N>=2, let U be the primes below pN with p removed. Splitting the full cofactor cube into labels with and without p gives

`Q_(P union {p})(pN)-Q_P(pN)=-2sqrt(p)*sum_(R subset U) F_(pN,P)(R)*F_(N,P)(R)`.

The square of the reflected copy cancels exactly with the removed p-containing fibre energy. The complete mixed inner product survives. No absolute values, sign assumption or endpoint bound replace it. This identity is proved at the exact integer dilation anchors pN with p>N; a general nonintegral quotient would additionally retain the clipped terminal block.

## Positive isolated fibres after smaller-prime processing

If P contains every prime below N, the smaller source is concentrated at its empty label. The retained singleton at p is then

`F_(pN,P)({p})=-sqrt(p)*S(N)`.

The already analytic seven-cutoff bounds prove `S(7)<0`. Taking P to be the primes below seven, namely2,3,5, gives a strictly positive singleton at every cutoff7p with prime p>7. These positive fibres exceed every fixed real bound beyond every cutoff, by square-root growth and the infinitude of primes. Processing that prime strictly increases the retained head.

The original prime coefficients are nonpositive by unsigned source positivity. Their retained orientation therefore need not survive earlier mergers. A blanket nonpositive-singleton extension of the late-prime rule is false for the actual source, cofinally. The positive survivor is the exact full-fibre recursion and its mixed energy law. The [late-prime endpoint theorem](ccm-fu-late-prime-block-endpoints.md) retains its stated common-sign, isolated-band scope.

structure GaussianArithmeticWidthCertificate (ε : ℝ) where

  compact_retained_ge_zero :

/-!
# Finite clipping-stable source margins on every retained prime field

Unconditional Landau separation supplies an actual source cutoff for every
nonzero retained direction. Compactness of the finite coordinate unit sphere
extracts finitely many cutoffs with one positive homogeneous margin. Finite
source-mass bounds preserve that margin under independent sufficiently small
adjacent-cutoff clipping. The pairing is exactly the coordinate pairing with
the complete source vector grouped by retained prime-intersection labels.
These witnesses depend on the retained field; cofinal energy propagation is
not asserted.
-/

noncomputable section
open Complex Set Metric
namespace RHTower

/-- All subsets of the finite retained prime field, including the empty label. -/
abbrev retainedPrimeFieldIndex (Q : Finset Nat.Primes) :=
  ↥((Q.image (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ))).powerset)

/-- Real coordinates of a functional on the complete finite retained field. -/
abbrev retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates (Q : Finset Nat.Primes) := retainedPrimeFieldIndex Q → ℝ

private def retainedFieldExtension (Q : Finset Nat.Primes)
    (z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) (R : Finset ℕ) : ℝ :=
  if h : R ∈ (Q.image (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ))).powerset then z ⟨R, h⟩ else 0

/-- Pairing with the complete actual retained field at one source cutoff. -/
def retainedPrimeFieldPairing (Q : Finset Nat.Primes)
    (z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) (M : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 M,
    z ⟨d.primeFactors ∩ Q.image (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ)),
      Finset.mem_powerset.mpr Finset.inter_subset_right⟩ * mobiusDivisorDilationChannel M d

private lemma fieldPairing_eq_sourceMean (Q : Finset Nat.Primes)
    (z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) (M : ℕ) :
    retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z M =
      (retainedPrimeSourceMean (Q.image (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ)))
        (fun R => (retainedFieldExtension Q z R : ℂ)) M).re := by
  simp [retainedPrimeFieldPairing, retainedPrimeSourceMean, retainedFieldExtension,
    Finset.mem_powerset.mpr Finset.inter_subset_right]

lemma continuous_retainedPrimeFieldPairing (Q : Finset Nat.Primes) (M : ℕ) :
    Continuous (fun z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q => retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z M) := by
  unfold retainedPrimeFieldPairing
  fun_prop

lemma retainedPrimeFieldPairing_smul (Q : Finset Nat.Primes)
    (z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) (c : ℝ) (M : ℕ) :
    retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q (c • z) M = c * retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z M := by
  simp [retainedPrimeFieldPairing, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc]

/-- Every nonzero direction in the complete retained field is strictly detected
by an actual source cutoff. -/
lemma exists_positive_retainedPrimeFieldPairing (Q : Finset Nat.Primes)
    (z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) (hz : z ≠ 0) :
    ∃ M : ℕ, 0 < retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z M := by
  have hcoord : ∃ R : retainedPrimeFieldIndex Q, z R ≠ 0 := by
    by_contra hn
    push Not at hn
    apply hz
    funext R
    exact hn R
  obtain ⟨R, hR⟩ := hcoord
  have hy : ∃ S : Finset ℕ, S ⊆ Q.image (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ)) ∧
      retainedFieldExtension Q z S ≠ 0 := by
    refine ⟨R.1, Finset.mem_powerset.mp R.2, ?_⟩
    simpa only [retainedFieldExtension, dif_pos R.2] using hR
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := exists_positive_retainedPrimeSourceMean Q (retainedFieldExtension Q z) hy
  exact ⟨M, by rwa [fieldPairing_eq_sourceMean]⟩

/-- Each finite retained field has a finite family of actual source cutoffs and
one uniform positive directional margin. The cutoffs depend on the retained field. -/
theorem exists_retainedPrimeField_finite_uniform_margin (Q : Finset Nat.Primes) :
    ∃ K : Finset ℕ, K.Nonempty ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
      ∀ z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q, ∃ M ∈ K,
        c * ‖z‖ ≤ retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z M := by
  letI : Nonempty (retainedPrimeFieldIndex Q) := ⟨⟨∅, by simp⟩⟩
  let S := sphere (0 : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) 1
  have hS : IsCompact S := isCompact_sphere _ _
  have hSne : S.Nonempty := by
    refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
    simp [S]
  let U : ℕ → Set (retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) := fun M =>
    {z | 0 < retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z M}
  have hU : ∀ M, IsOpen (U M) := fun M =>
    isOpen_lt continuous_const (continuous_retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q M)
  have hcover : S ⊆ ⋃ M, U M := by
    intro z hz
    have hn : ‖z‖ = 1 := by simpa only [S, mem_sphere, dist_zero_right] using hz
    have hz0 : z ≠ 0 := by intro he; simp [he] at hn
    obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := exists_positive_retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z hz0
    exact mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨M, hM⟩
  obtain ⟨K, hKcover⟩ := hS.elim_finite_subcover U hU hcover
  have hK : K.Nonempty := by
    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hSne
    obtain ⟨M, hM, _⟩ := mem_iUnion₂.mp (hKcover hz)
    exact ⟨M, hM⟩
  let F : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q → ℝ := fun z =>

This module expands every cutoff-centered eta moment in the finite-window
energy ledger into the literal logarithmic intervals retained by the paired
eta measure.  The uncompleted Gram kernel is consequently an exact finite
triple sum over cutoff coordinates and pairs of arithmetic intervals.

The expansion is propagated through the fixed completion weights, the
diagonal and distinct-zero masses, and the terminal multiplicity-aware
rank--trace ledger.  No sign or cancellation estimate for the resulting
interval correlation is assumed or proved here.

open Complex Filter MeasureTheory Metric Set Topology

  Topology

/-- The order-`k` centered Laplace contribution from the `n`th retained
logarithmic eta interval. -/
def pairedEtaLogLaplaceCenteredMomentIntervalAtom
    (k : ℕ) (s : ℂ) (a : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  ∫ t : ℝ in Real.log (2 * n + 1)..Real.log (2 * n + 2),
    (((t - a : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ k) * Complex.exp (-s * t)

/-- A finite centered eta moment is exactly the sum of its retained interval
atoms. -/
theorem pairedEtaLogLaplaceMomentCenteredPartialSum_eq_sum_intervalAtoms
    (k N : ℕ) (s : ℂ) (a : ℝ) :
    pairedEtaLogLaplaceMomentCenteredPartialSum k s a N =
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N,
        pairedEtaLogLaplaceCenteredMomentIntervalAtom k s a n := by
  rw [pairedEtaLogLaplaceMomentCenteredPartialSum_eq_integral_finiteLogMeasure]
  unfold pairedEtaFiniteLogMeasure
  rw [integral_finsetSum_measure]
  · apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro n _hn
    unfold pairedEtaLogLaplaceCenteredMomentIntervalAtom
    rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_of_le
      (pairedEtaFiniteLogInterval_pos n).le]
  · intro n _hn
    change IntegrableOn (fun t : ℝ ↦
      (((t - a : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ k) * Complex.exp (-s * t))
      (Ioc (Real.log (2 * n + 1)) (Real.log (2 * n + 2)))
    apply IntegrableOn.mono_set
      ((show Continuous (fun t : ℝ ↦
        (((t - a : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ k) * Complex.exp (-s * t)) by
          fun_prop).continuousOn.integrableOn_Icc)
    exact Ioc_subset_Icc_self

/-- The literal retained-interval atom in the top-prefix centered moment at a
nontrivial zero. -/
def pairedEtaTopPrefixFiniteCenteredIntervalAtom
    (rho : NontrivialZetaZero) (N n : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  pairedEtaLogLaplaceCenteredMomentIntervalAtom
    (analyticZetaZeroMultiplicity rho - 1) rho.1
      (pairedEtaLogTailCutoff (N + 1)) n

/-- The top-prefix centered moment is exactly its finite sum of literal eta
interval atoms. -/
theorem pairedEtaTopPrefixFiniteCenteredMoment_eq_sum_intervalAtoms
    (rho : NontrivialZetaZero) (N : ℕ) :
    pairedEtaTopPrefixFiniteCenteredMoment rho N =
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1),
        pairedEtaTopPrefixFiniteCenteredIntervalAtom rho N n := by
  simpa only [pairedEtaTopPrefixFiniteCenteredMoment,
    pairedEtaLogLaplaceMomentCutoffCenteredPartialSum,
    pairedEtaTopPrefixFiniteCenteredIntervalAtom, pairedEtaLogTailCutoff] using
      (pairedEtaLogLaplaceMomentCenteredPartialSum_eq_sum_intervalAtoms

/-- The literal cutoff/interval expansion of the uncompleted finite eta
moment correlation. -/

/-- The finite moment Gram kernel is exactly the finite cutoff/interval
triple correlation. -/
theorem pairedEtaTopPrefixFiniteCutoffFamilyMomentCorrelation_eq_intervalCorrelation

    (sigma rho : NontrivialZetaZero) :

        cutoff sigma rho := by

    pairedEtaTopPrefixFiniteCutoffFamilyIntervalCorrelation

  intro j _hj
  rw [pairedEtaTopPrefixFiniteCenteredMoment_eq_sum_intervalAtoms,

/-!
# Multiplicative domain of the logarithmic Sonin clock

The finite-clock multiplicative-domain theorem specializes to logarithmic Fourier scattering.
The complete Sonin star-Kadison defect is the twirled master constraint of the observable
component erased by scattering, and it vanishes exactly on the scattering commutant.

Unlike the earlier squared Sonin Kadison defect, this result applies to arbitrary transition
operators: no self-adjointness, positivity, or physical-state hypothesis remains.
-/

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Complete star-Kadison defect of the logarithmic Sonin clock-observer projection. -/
def soninLogFourierObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect
    (X : SoninL2 →L[ℂ] SoninL2) : SoninL2 →L[ℂ] SoninL2 :=
  HTGeometry.finiteCyclicObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect
    soninLogFourierScattering X 2

/-- The logarithmic Sonin observable twirl preserves adjoints for arbitrary operators. -/
theorem soninLogFourierObservableTwirl_adjoint
    (X : SoninL2 →L[ℂ] SoninL2) :
    (soninLogFourierObservableTwirl X).adjoint =
      soninLogFourierObservableTwirl X.adjoint := by
  simpa only [soninLogFourierObservableTwirl] using
    HTGeometry.finiteCyclicObservableTwirl_adjoint
      soninLogFourierScattering X 2 two_ne_zero
      soninLogFourierScattering_adjoint_mul_self
      soninLogFourierScattering_sq_eq_one

/-- **Sonin operator-valued conditional variance.**  The complete clock defect is the Sonin
twirl of the master constraint of the scattering-erased observable component. -/
theorem soninLogFourierObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect_eq_twirl_quantumMasterConstraint
    (X : SoninL2 →L[ℂ] SoninL2) :
    soninLogFourierObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect X =
      soninLogFourierObservableTwirl
        (HTGeometry.quantumMasterConstraint
          (X - soninLogFourierObservableTwirl X)) := by
  simpa only [soninLogFourierObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect,
    soninLogFourierObservableTwirl] using
      HTGeometry.finiteCyclicObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect_eq_twirl_quantumMasterConstraint
        soninLogFourierScattering X 2 two_ne_zero
        soninLogFourierScattering_adjoint_mul_self
        soninLogFourierScattering_sq_eq_one

/-- The complete Sonin clock defect vanishes exactly when scattering erases no observable
component. -/
theorem soninLogFourierObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect_eq_zero_iff_twirl_fixed
    (X : SoninL2 →L[ℂ] SoninL2) :
    soninLogFourierObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect X = 0 ↔
      soninLogFourierObservableTwirl X = X := by
  simpa only [soninLogFourierObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect,
    soninLogFourierObservableTwirl] using
      HTGeometry.finiteCyclicObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect_eq_zero_iff_twirl_fixed
        soninLogFourierScattering X 2 two_ne_zero
        soninLogFourierScattering_adjoint_mul_self
        soninLogFourierScattering_sq_eq_one

/-- **Sonin multiplicative-domain theorem.**  For every bounded operator, zero complete
conditional variance is equivalent to commutation with logarithmic Fourier scattering. -/
theorem soninLogFourierObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect_eq_zero_iff_commutes
    (X : SoninL2 →L[ℂ] SoninL2) :
    soninLogFourierObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect X = 0 ↔
      soninLogFourierScattering * X = X * soninLogFourierScattering := by
  simpa only [soninLogFourierObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect] using
    HTGeometry.finiteCyclicObservableTwirlStarKadisonDefect_eq_zero_iff_commutes
      soninLogFourierScattering X 2 two_ne_zero
      soninLogFourierScattering_adjoint_mul_self
      soninLogFourierScattering_sq_eq_one

end

/-!
# Connes--Consani residue perturbation capstone

This module combines the trace-class modulus-square reduction with logarithmic-residue stability.
If a compact distinguished block has a weak Schatten-one measurable modulus square, then adding any
trace-class remainder preserves both weak Schatten-one membership and the exact logarithmic residue
of the modulus square.  No positivity, compactness, or ideal premise on the full modulus square is
left to the caller.
-/

namespace RHTower

open ContinuousLinearMap

noncomputable section

variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]

/-- A trace-class perturbation of a compact block preserves weak trace-ideal membership and the
exact measurable logarithmic residue of its modulus square. -/
theorem weakAndHasSchattenLogResidue_modulusSq_add_traceClass
    {E R : H →L[ℂ] H} (hEcpt : IsCompactOperator E) (hR : IsTraceClass R) {Q : ℝ}
    (hweak : MemWeakSchattenClass 1 (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint E ∘L E))
    (hres : HasSchattenLogResidue 1 (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint E ∘L E) Q) :
    MemWeakSchattenClass 1
        (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (E + R) ∘L (E + R)) ∧
      HasSchattenLogResidue 1
        (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (E + R) ∘L (E + R)) Q := by
  have hRmem : MemSchattenClass 1 R := IsTraceClass.memSchattenClass_one hR
  have hRcpt : IsCompactOperator R := hRmem.isCompactOperator one_pos
  have hERcpt : IsCompactOperator (E + R) := hEcpt.add hRcpt
  have hBcpt : IsCompactOperator (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint E ∘L E) :=
    energyOp_compact hEcpt
  have hAcpt : IsCompactOperator
      (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (E + R) ∘L (E + R)) :=
    energyOp_compact hERcpt
  have hBpos : 0 ≤ ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint E ∘L E := by
    apply CStarAlgebra.nonneg_iff_eq_star_mul_self.mpr
    exact ⟨E, rfl⟩
  have hApos : 0 ≤ ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (E + R) ∘L (E + R) := by
    apply CStarAlgebra.nonneg_iff_eq_star_mul_self.mpr
    exact ⟨E + R, rfl⟩
  have hdiff : MemSchattenClass 1
      (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (E + R) ∘L (E + R) -
        ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint E ∘L E) :=
    memSchattenClass_one_modulusSq_sub hR
  exact weakAndHasSchattenLogResidue_one_of_nonneg_traceClass_sub
    hAcpt hBcpt hApos hBpos hdiff hweak hres

end

end RHTower

/-!
# The true Sonin Fourier constraint in logarithmic coordinates

Normalized dilations become translations under the exact even logarithmic
unitary, but the Sonin Fourier transform does not become the ordinary Fourier
transform in that coordinate.  Its conjugate is an involutive scattering
operator which reverses translations.

The distinction is forced by the orbital-length commutator.  Multiplication by
`log |x|` has scalar commutator `-log p` with normalized dilation by `p`, whereas
ordinary position has an `x`-dependent commutator and cannot produce any scalar
orbital length.  Thus a Sonin realization of the Euler logarithm must carry the
Mellin-scattering/Burnol conductor channel; the ordinary-position two-edge
Fourier-cutoff calculation is not that channel.
-/

open Complex

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- The original Fourier involution conjugated through the exact even
logarithmic-coordinate unitary. -/
def soninLogFourierScattering : SoninL2 →L[ℂ] SoninL2 :=
  logEvenUnitary.toLinearIsometry.toContinuousLinearMap ∘L
    evenFourierTransform ∘L
      logEvenUnitary.symm.toLinearIsometry.toContinuousLinearMap

@[simp] theorem soninLogFourierScattering_apply (g : SoninL2) :
    soninLogFourierScattering g =
      logEvenUnitary (evenFourierTransform (logEvenUnitary.symm g)) := rfl

/-- Original Fourier inversion sends physical dilation by `p` to dilation by
`p⁻¹`, also on the even carrier. -/
theorem evenFourierTransform_evenDilation
    (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (f : evenSubspace) :
    evenFourierTransform (evenDilationUnitary p hp f) =
      evenDilationUnitary p⁻¹ (inv_pos.mpr hp) (evenFourierTransform f) := by
  apply Subtype.ext
  exact fourierUnitary_dilation p hp f

/-- The logarithmic-coordinate Sonin Fourier scattering is an involution. -/
@[simp] theorem soninLogFourierScattering_involutive (g : SoninL2) :
    soninLogFourierScattering (soninLogFourierScattering g) = g := by
  change logEvenUnitary
      (evenFourierTransform
        (logEvenUnitary.symm
          (logEvenUnitary
            (evenFourierTransform (logEvenUnitary.symm g))))) = g
  rw [logEvenUnitary.symm_apply_apply, evenFourierTransform_involutive,
    logEvenUnitary.apply_symm_apply]

/-- The logarithmic-coordinate Sonin Fourier scattering preserves the Hilbert norm. -/
theorem soninLogFourierScattering_norm (g : SoninL2) :
    ‖soninLogFourierScattering g‖ = ‖g‖ := by
  rw [soninLogFourierScattering_apply, logEvenUnitary.norm_map,
    evenFourierTransform_isometry, logEvenUnitary.symm.norm_map]

/-- Operator form of the unitarity of logarithmic Sonin Fourier scattering. -/
theorem soninLogFourierScattering_adjoint_mul_self :
    soninLogFourierScattering.adjoint * soninLogFourierScattering = 1 := by
  simpa only [ContinuousLinearMap.mul_def] using
    (ContinuousLinearMap.norm_map_iff_adjoint_comp_self
      soninLogFourierScattering).mp soninLogFourierScattering_norm

/-- Operator form of the existing involution relation. -/
theorem soninLogFourierScattering_sq_eq_one :
    soninLogFourierScattering ^ 2 = 1 := by
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
  intro g
  change soninLogFourierScattering (soninLogFourierScattering g) = g
  exact soninLogFourierScattering_involutive g

/-- The involutive unitary logarithmic scattering is self-adjoint. -/
theorem soninLogFourierScattering_isSelfAdjoint :
    IsSelfAdjoint soninLogFourierScattering :=
  HTGeometry.isSelfAdjoint_of_adjoint_mul_self_of_sq_eq_one
    soninLogFourierScattering soninLogFourierScattering_adjoint_mul_self
    soninLogFourierScattering_sq_eq_one

/-- **Sonin optical-theorem collapse.**  The positive master constraint of logarithmic Fourier
scattering is not a new quadratic operator: involutive unitarity reduces it exactly to twice the
anti-invariant scattering sector. -/
theorem quantumMasterConstraint_soninLogFourierScattering_eq_two_mul_complement :
    HTGeometry.quantumMasterConstraint (soninLogFourierScattering - 1) =
      2 * (1 - soninLogFourierScattering) := by
  exact HTGeometry.quantumMasterConstraint_involutiveScattering_eq_two_mul_complement
    soninLogFourierScattering soninLogFourierScattering_adjoint_mul_self
    soninLogFourierScattering_sq_eq_one

/-- The `Z₂` group average selecting the invariant logarithmic Sonin scattering sector. -/
def soninLogFourierInvariantAverage : SoninL2 →L[ℂ] SoninL2 :=
  HTGeometry.finiteCyclicGaugeAverage soninLogFourierScattering 2

/-- The invariant-sector average is an orthogonal projection: its self-adjointness no longer has
to be supplied as a downstream hypothesis. -/
theorem soninLogFourierInvariantAverage_isSelfAdjoint :
    IsSelfAdjoint soninLogFourierInvariantAverage := by

t a p ha hp
  exact (centralSoninRelativeGramLinearCross_isHilbertSchmidt a p ha hp).add
    (hR.adjoint.comp_right (centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp))

/-- A relative Gram defect is self-adjoint before any trace or spectral interpretation. -/
theorem adjoint_centralSoninRelativeGramDefect
    (a p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (centralSoninRelativeGramDefect a p hp) =
      centralSoninRelativeGramDefect a p hp := by

    sonin_adjoint_mul, sonin_adjoint_mul, adjoint_adjoint, adjoint_adjoint]

/-- Principal-relative Gram defect after weighting the actual residual by `c`. -/
def centralSoninWeightedRelativeGramDefect
    (a p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) (c : Complex) : SoninL2 →L[Complex] SoninL2 :=
  let P := centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp
  let R := centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp
  ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (P + c • R) * (P + c • R) -
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint P * P

/-- **Linear Euler interface.**  The principal-relative defect contains `c` and `star c`
linearly; only its residual energy uses the squared coefficient `star c * c`. -/
theorem centralSoninWeightedRelativeGramDefect_eq
    (a p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) (c : Complex) :
    centralSoninWeightedRelativeGramDefect a p hp c =
      c • (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
          (centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp) *
            centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp) +
      star c • (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
          (centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp) *
            centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp) +
      (star c * c) • centralSoninDilationCornerResidualEnergy a p hp := by
  let P := centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp
  let R := centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp
  simp only [centralSoninWeightedRelativeGramDefect,
    centralSoninDilationCornerResidualEnergy]
  change ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (P + c • R) * (P + c • R) -
      ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint P * P =
    c • (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint P * R) +
      star c • (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint R * P) +
        (star c * c) • (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint R * R)
  rw [sonin_adjoint_add, sonin_adjoint_smul]
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
  intro x
  simp only [mul_apply_eq_comp, _root_.add_apply,
    _root_.sub_apply, _root_.smul_apply, map_add, map_smul]
  module

/-- Weighting does not reintroduce a Schatten hypothesis: the full relative defect remains
Hilbert--Schmidt for every scalar coefficient. -/
theorem centralSoninWeightedRelativeGramDefect_isHilbertSchmidt
    (a p : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hp : 1 < p) (c : Complex) :
    IsHilbertSchmidt (centralSoninWeightedRelativeGramDefect a p hp c) := by
  rw [centralSoninWeightedRelativeGramDefect_eq]
  have hR := centralSoninDilationCornerResidual_isHilbertSchmidt a p ha hp
  exact ((hR.comp_left
      (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp))).smul c).add
    ((hR.adjoint.comp_right
      (centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp)).smul (star c)) |>.add
      ((hR.adjoint.comp_right
        (centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp)).smul (star c * c))

/-- The principal-relative Gram defect at the actual prime-power scale, weighted by the exact
logarithmic Euler coefficient used by the Sonin tail. -/
def centralSoninPrimePowerRelativeGramDefect
    (a : ℝ) (pk : Nat.Primes × ℕ) : SoninL2 →L[Complex] SoninL2 :=
  centralSoninWeightedRelativeGramDefect a (soninPrimePowerScale pk)
    (one_lt_soninPrimePowerScale pk) (soninLogPrimePowerCoefficient pk)

/-- The prime-power relative defect is Hilbert--Schmidt with no source hypothesis. -/
theorem centralSoninPrimePowerRelativeGramDefect_isHilbertSchmidt
    (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (pk : Nat.Primes × ℕ) :
    IsHilbertSchmidt (centralSoninPrimePowerRelativeGramDefect a pk) := by
  exact centralSoninWeightedRelativeGramDefect_isHilbertSchmidt a
    (soninPrimePowerScale pk) ha (one_lt_soninPrimePowerScale pk)
    (soninLogPrimePowerCoefficient pk)

/-- At every prime power the relative defect exposes the unsquared logarithmic coefficient in
its two principal/residual cross terms.  The coefficient is squared only in the final
trace-class residual energy. -/
theorem centralSoninPrimePowerRelativeGramDefect_eq
    (a : ℝ) (pk : Nat.Primes × ℕ) :
    centralSoninPrimePowerRelativeGramDefect a pk =
      soninLogPrimePowerCoefficient pk •
        (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
          (centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a (soninPrimePowerScale pk)
            (one_lt_soninPrimePowerScale pk)) *
          centralSoninPrimePowerResidual a pk) +
      star (soninLogPrimePowerCoefficient pk) •
        (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (centralSoninPrimePowerResidual a pk) *
          centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a (soninPrimePowerScale pk)
            (one_lt_soninPrimePowerScale pk)) +
      (star (soninLogPrimePowerCoefficient pk) * soninLogPrimePowerCoefficient pk) •

/-
# The principal-relative Sonin Gram defect

The residual Gram `R†R` squares every Euler coefficient and therefore cannot by itself recover
the logarithmic prime modes.  The relative Gram defect keeps the principal corner `P`:

`(P + cR)†(P + cR) - P†P
  = c P†R + star(c) R†P + star(c)c R†R`.

Thus the actual Sonin source has a canonical term linear in the logarithmic Euler coefficient.
The whole defect is Hilbert--Schmidt without an extra hypothesis; only the quadratic remainder is
automatically trace class.  Producing a scalar relative trace from the linear cross term remains
the source-side open core.
-/

private theorem sonin_adjoint_add
    (S T : SoninL2 →L[Complex] SoninL2) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (S + T) =
      ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint S + ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T := by
  let adj : (SoninL2 →L[Complex] SoninL2) ≃ₗᵢ⋆[Complex]
      (SoninL2 →L[Complex] SoninL2) := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
  exact adj.map_add S T

private theorem sonin_adjoint_sub
    (S T : SoninL2 →L[Complex] SoninL2) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (S - T) =
      ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint S - ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T := by
  let adj : (SoninL2 →L[Complex] SoninL2) ≃ₗᵢ⋆[Complex]
      (SoninL2 →L[Complex] SoninL2) := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
  exact adj.map_sub S T

private theorem sonin_adjoint_mul
    (S T : SoninL2 →L[Complex] SoninL2) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (S * T) =
      ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T * ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint S := by
  exact ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp S T

theorem sonin_adjoint_smul (c : Complex)
    (T : SoninL2 →L[Complex] SoninL2) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (c • T) =
      star c • ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T := by
  change star (c • T) = star c • star T
  rw [star_smul]

/-- Difference between the actual one-scale Sonin Gram and the formal-principal Gram. -/
def centralSoninRelativeGramDefect
    (a p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) : SoninL2 →L[Complex] SoninL2 :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
      (crossBoundary (centralSoninProjection a) (dilationSum p hp)) *
      crossBoundary (centralSoninProjection a) (dilationSum p hp) -
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp) *
      centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp

/-- The part of the relative Gram defect which is linear in the principal-subtracted residual. -/
def centralSoninRelativeGramLinearCross
    (a p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) : SoninL2 →L[Complex] SoninL2 :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp) *
      centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp +
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp) *
      centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp

/-- Exact principal-linear/quadratic decomposition of the unweighted relative Gram defect. -/
theorem centralSoninRelativeGramDefect_eq_linearCross_add_energy
    (a p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) :
    centralSoninRelativeGramDefect a p hp =
      centralSoninRelativeGramLinearCross a p hp +
        centralSoninDilationCornerResidualEnergy a p hp := by
  let A := crossBoundary (centralSoninProjection a) (dilationSum p hp)
  let P := centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp
  let R := centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp
  have hA : A = R + P := by
    simp only [A, R, centralSoninDilationCornerResidual]
    abel
  simp only [centralSoninRelativeGramDefect,
    centralSoninRelativeGramLinearCross,
    centralSoninDilationCornerResidualEnergy]
  change ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A * A - ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint P * P =
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint P * R + ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint R * P +
      ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint R * R
  rw [hA, sonin_adjoint_add]
  noncomm_ring

/-- The principal/residual cross term is unconditionally Hilbert--Schmidt. -/
theorem centralSoninRelativeGramLinearCross_isHilbertSchmidt
    (a p : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hp : 1 < p) :
    IsHilbertSchmidt (centralSoninRelativeGramLinearCross a p hp) := by
  have hR := centralSoninDilationCornerResidual_isHilbertSchmidt a p ha hp
  exact (hR.comp_left
    (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp))).add
    (hR.adjoint.comp_right (centralSoninPrincipalDilationCorner a p hp))

/-- The full relative Gram defect is unconditionally Hilbert--Schmidt. -/
theorem centralSoninRelativeGramDefect_isHilbertSchmidt
    (a p : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hp : 1 < p) :
    IsHilbertSchmidt (centralSoninRelativeGramDefect a p hp) := by
  rw [centralSoninRelativeGramDefect_eq_linearCross_add_energy]
  have hR := centralSoninDilationCornerResidual_isHilbertSchmidt a p ha hp
  exact (centralSoninRelativeGramLinearCross_isHilbertSchmidt a p ha hp).add
    (hR.adjoint.comp_right (centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp))

source_arguments.statement:

    Function.Injective rightHalfPlaneLSeriesToUpperEndAnalytic
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem rightHalfPlaneLSeriesToUpperEndAnalytic_injective :
    Function.Injective rightHalfPlaneLSeriesToUpperEndAnalytic
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  intro f g hfg
  have hgerm := congrArg Subtype.val hfg
  change Germ.coeRingHom upperEndFilter
      (fun z : ℂ => LSeries (fun n => f.1 n) (-Complex.I * z)) =
    Germ.coeRingHom upperEndFilter
      (fun z : ℂ => LSeries (fun n => g.1 n) (-Complex.I * z)) at hgerm
  change (↑(fun z : ℂ => LSeries (fun n => f.1 n) (-Complex.I * z)) :
      Germ upperEndFilter ℂ) =
    (↑(fun z : ℂ => LSeries (fun n => g.1 n) (-Complex.I * z)) :
      Germ upperEndFilter ℂ) at hgerm
  rw [Germ.coe_eq] at hgerm
  change ∀ᶠ z in upperEndFilter,
    LSeries (fun n => f.1 n) (-Complex.I * z) =
      LSeries (fun n => g.1 n) (-Complex.I * z) at hgerm
  rw [upperEndFilter_basis.eventually_iff] at hgerm
  obtain ⟨H, -, hH⟩ := hgerm
  have hevent : (fun x : ℝ => LSeries (fun n => f.1 n) (x : ℂ)) =ᶠ[atTop]
      (fun x : ℝ => LSeries (fun n => g.1 n) (x : ℂ)) := by
    filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop H] with x hx
    have hz := hH (show Complex.I * (x : ℂ) ∈ upperTail H by
      simpa [upperTail, Complex.mul_im] using hx)
    have hrot : -Complex.I * (Complex.I * (x : ℂ)) = (x : ℂ) := by
      calc
        -Complex.I * (Complex.I * (x : ℂ)) =
            (-Complex.I * Complex.I) * (x : ℂ) := (mul_assoc _ _ _).symm
        _ = (x : ℂ) := by rw [neg_mul, Complex.I_mul_I]; ring
    simpa only [hrot] using hz
  apply Subtype.ext
  apply ArithmeticFunction.ext
  intro n
  by_cases hn : n = 0
  · subst n
    simp only [ArithmeticFunction.map_zero]
  · exact LSeries.eq_of_LSeries_eventually_eq
      ((rightHalfPlaneArithmeticSubalgebra_abscissa_le_one f).trans_lt
        (EReal.coe_lt_top (1 : ℝ)))
      ((rightHalfPlaneArithmeticSubalgebra_abscissa_le_one g).trans_lt
        (EReal.coe_lt_top (1 : ℝ)))
      hevent hn

# Dense-resolvent transpose purity

- **ID:** `deninger-dense-resolvent-transpose-purity`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper)
- **Label:** `DAC_DENSE_RESOLVENT_TRANSPOSE_PURITY`
- **Parent:** `deninger-arithmetic-calderon-paugam-hardy-comparison`
- **Statement:** a nonzero continuous transpose eigenfunctional on
  source cohomology forces failure of the corresponding resolvent on
  every dense invariant core; hence a Hodge core with off-axis
  resolvent stability forces weight-one purity without Riesz
  boundedness of the eigenfunctional.

## Goal

Replace pointwise Hilbert boundedness of Meyer evaluation functionals
by the natural rigged-Hilbert regularity condition: the Hodge
resolvent preserves a dense source core.  This is weaker, sees the
strong dual where Meyer's eigenvectors actually live, and reduces the
RH gate to a source elliptic-regularity theorem.

## Algebraic theorem

Let \(D\) be a complex vector space, let \(T:D\to D\) be linear, and
let \(\ell:D\to\mathbb C\) satisfy
\[
  \ell(Tx)=\lambda\ell(x) \qquad (x\in D).                 \tag{1}
\]
If
\[
  T-\lambda:D\longrightarrow D                            \tag{2}
\]
is surjective, then \(\ell=0\).

### Proof

`[PROVED HERE]`

For \(y\in D\), choose \(x\in D\) with
\((T-\lambda)x=y\).  Equation `(1)` gives
\[
  \ell(y)=\ell(Tx)-\lambda\ell(x)=0.
\]
Since \(y\) was arbitrary, \(\ell=0\).

## Dense-source theorem

Let \(E\) be a Hausdorff locally convex source cohomology space,
\(D\subset E\) a dense invariant vector subspace, and
\(\ell\in E'\) nonzero.  Continuity and density imply
\(\ell|_D\ne0\).  Therefore:

1. if \(\ell(Tx)=\lambda\ell(x)\) on \(D\), then
   \(T-\lambda\) is not surjective on \(D\);
2. if \(V:D\to D\) and
   \(\ell(Vx)=c\ell(x)\), then \(V-c\) is not surjective on \(D\).

Consequently, suppose a weight-one arithmetic Hodge realization has
centered generator
\[
  A=\Theta-\tfrac12
\]
and a dense source core \(D_{\mathrm{Hdg}}\) such that
\[
  A-z:D_{\mathrm{Hdg}}\longrightarrow D_{\mathrm{Hdg}}
  \quad\text{is surjective whenever }\operatorname{Re}z\ne0. \tag{3}
\]
Every nonzero continuous transpose eigenfunctional of \(\Theta\) has
eigenvalue \(\rho\) with
\[
  \operatorname{Re}\rho=\tfrac12.                         \tag{4}
\]

Alternatively, for the centered time-one flow \(V=e^A\), it is enough
to prove
\[
  V-c:D_{\mathrm{Hdg}}\longrightarrow D_{\mathrm{Hdg}}
  \quad\text{is surjective whenever }|c|\ne1.              \tag{5}
\]
Then every nonzero transpose eigencharacter has modulus one.  For
\(c=e^{\rho-1/2}\), this again gives `(4)`.

## Why this improves the RH gate

Meyer's generalized zero states are continuous functionals on the
strong dual of the nuclear quotient; they need not be vectors in the
Hodge Hilbert space.  The earlier Riesz criterion requires each
order-zero state to extend boundedly to the Hilbert completion.  The
dense-resolvent criterion requires only:

1. a source-defined dense smooth Hodge core;
2. invariance of that core under the centered flow;
3. source regularity of the off-axis Hodge resolvent.

These conditions are standard outputs of elliptic Hodge theory.  In
the arithmetic setting they must be proved for the global
Calderón--Green intermediate extension and its strict nuclear limit.
No zeta zero is used to define the core or resolvent.

## Generalized jets

The same argument handles a finite Jordan chain.  If
\((T'-\lambda)^m\ell=0\) and \(T-\lambda\) is surjective on the core,
then every power \((T-\lambda)^m\) is surjective.  Applying the
algebraic theorem inductively forces \(\ell=0\).  Thus dense resolvent
stability excludes every off-axis generalized Meyer block, not only
order-zero states.

# Kähler--Riemann arithmetic leaf realization

- **ID:** `deninger-kahler-riemann-arithmetic-leaf-realization`
- **Stage:** 1-in-progress
- **Type:** SOURCE CONJECTURE
- **Label:** `DAC_KAHLER_RIEMANN_ARITHMETIC_LEAF_REALIZATION`
- **Parent:** `deninger-arithmetic-cohomology-construction`
- **Statement:** the coarse invariant arithmetic coefficient is the
  derived pushforward of a complex
  two-real-dimensional Kähler--Riemann leaf complex whose transverse
  flow conformally scales the leaf metric and whose degree-one
  cohomology is odd in \(K_{\mathbb R}\); its all-number-fields
  extension is genuinely quaternionically twisted.

## Why this is the correct positivity gate

Deninger's formalism requires a positive Hodge star and
\(\Theta_1-\tfrac12\) skew-adjoint.  Deninger--Singhof prove both
conclusions for reduced cohomology once one has a dense-leaf
Kähler--Riemann foliation and a flow satisfying
\[
 (\phi^t)^*[\omega]=e^t[\omega].
\]
Therefore arithmetic positivity should not be imposed directly on a
zero-indexed Hilbert space.  It should be derived from a source leaf
metric.

Deninger's rational-Witt system is an approximation and its character
leaves are not known to be closed two-dimensional Riemannian leaves.  A
geometric refinement, or an equivalent sheaf-theoretic Hilbert complex,
is required.

The positive-radius refinement is now constructed globally.
`DAC_DENINGER_HILBERT_KUMMER_RADIAL_SUSPENSION` constructs the
source-defined radius
\[
 x([P,u])=u\|\ell_P\|.
\]
`DAC_EQUIVARIANT_RADIUS_ORBIT_TRIVIALIZATION` proves that every
positive equivariant radius globally splits its flow space as
\(x^{-1}(1)\times\mathbb R_{>0}\).  Its canonical half-density circle
refinement
\[
 \{(p,z):|z|^2=x(p)\}
 \cong x^{-1}(1)\times\mathbb C^\times
\]
has complex leaves, flow \(z\mapsto e^{t/2}z\), Kähler form scaling by
\(e^t\), Meyer's exact critical radial measure, and positive
degree-one Hodge star of square \(-1\).  No identification with the
unitary-character phase or Gamma-rank regular representation is used.
That orbit collar has tangent flow and is only a local metric model.

`DAC_HILBERT_KUMMER_AFFINE_LEAF_DISTRIBUTION` now constructs the
generic arithmetic foliation itself.  Its leaf frame is the modulus
Euler field \(A\) and Kummer--Kronecker phase field \(K\), with
\([A,K]=K\).  Deninger's flow changes suspension height, is transverse
to these leaves, and scales their Kähler form by \(e^t\).
`DAC_RESIDUAL_DENSE_KUMMER_LEAVES` proves that a dense \(G_\delta\) of
Kummer directions has dense phase leaves by Baire category and
Pontryagin duality.  Thus generic leaf dimension, transverse flow,
residual density, local Hodge positivity, and critical radial measure
are source-proved.  `DAC_PRO_LOG_KUMMER_CUSP_HODGE_EXTENSION`
continues the conformal star over every prime log collar, and
`DAC_REAL_ORIENTATION_TWISTED_HODGE_APEX` supplies the forced
orientation-sign descent at infinity.
`DAC_AFFINE_PRO_LOG_PRIME_HODGE_OVERLAP` closes mixed
generic/prime oriented-conformal gluing.  Global closed-complex
gluing must use a relative/rigged domain.
`DAC_ARITHMETIC_EXTENDED_CUSP_HODGE_BOUNDARY` now constructs the
prime extended-\(L^2\) domain retaining \(d\log z\), while
`DAC_KUMMER_RELATIVE_CALDERON_POISSON_DOMAIN` constructs the exact
relative Calderón domain at the unitary face.  Their global
Tate--Milnor incidence closure, Green supertrace comparison, and
harmonic faithfulness remain.

Deninger's no-real-coefficients theorem adds a non-negotiable
full-theory constraint: ordinary complexified real leafwise cohomology
cannot be the arithmetic \(H^1\) functorially for all number fields.
For the single \(\mathbb Q\) object, an additional real form is not
excluded; what is mandatory is an odd \(K_{\mathbb R}\) operator
\(J^2=-1\).  The all-number-fields extension must carry genuinely
quaternionic descent with no functorial real reduction.

## Exact twisted analytic interface

Benameur--Heitsch's twisted harmonic-signature theorem applies to an
oriented even-dimensional Riemannian foliation of a compact manifold
with a leafwise flat complex bundle \(E\) carrying a nondegenerate
Hermitian metric preserved by the leafwise flat connection.  Their
leafwise Hodge lemma identifies harmonic forms with reduced
\(L^2\)-cohomology.  Their transverse regularity theorem says that the
harmonic projection on the homotopy groupoid is transversely smooth
when leafwise parallel translation is bounded; this holds in particular
when the preserved Hermitian metric is positive definite.

This theorem supplies the analytic Hodge decomposition and smooth
harmonic projector once the arithmetic coefficient exists.  It does
not construct that coefficient, the rational-Witt leaf refinement, the
conformal flow, comparison `(1)`, or the Poisson--zeta cup pairing.
Those remain source obligations below.

/-!
# Coefficientwise Dirichlet-character twists

This file supplies the exact algebraic twist operation needed for Selberg-class factorization.
Twisting is a homomorphism for Dirichlet convolution and composes by multiplication of
characters.  Applying the inverse character does not generally recover the original arithmetic
function: it produces the principal-character depletion, erasing precisely the coefficients whose
indices are not coprime to the modulus.
-/

open Complex

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Coefficientwise twist of an arithmetic function by a Dirichlet character. -/
def dirichletCharacterTwist {q : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) : ArithmeticFunction ℂ where
  toFun n := χ (n : ZMod q) * f n
  map_zero' := by simp

@[simp]
theorem dirichletCharacterTwist_apply {q : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) (n : ℕ) :
    dirichletCharacterTwist χ f n = χ (n : ZMod q) * f n := rfl

/-- Retain exactly the coefficients whose indices are coprime to `q`. -/
def characterLevelDepletion (q : ℕ) (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) : ArithmeticFunction ℂ :=
  dirichletCharacterTwist (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) f

/-- Level depletion fixes every coefficient whose index is coprime to the level. -/
theorem characterLevelDepletion_apply_of_coprime {q n : ℕ} (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ)
    (hn : n.Coprime q) : characterLevelDepletion q f n = f n := by
  rw [characterLevelDepletion, dirichletCharacterTwist_apply,
    MulChar.one_apply ((ZMod.isUnit_iff_coprime n q).2 hn), one_mul]

/-- Level depletion erases every coefficient whose index is not coprime to the level. -/
theorem characterLevelDepletion_apply_of_not_coprime {q n : ℕ} (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ)
    (hn : ¬n.Coprime q) : characterLevelDepletion q f n = 0 := by
  rw [characterLevelDepletion, dirichletCharacterTwist_apply,
    MulChar.map_nonunit _ ((ZMod.isUnit_iff_coprime n q).not.mpr hn), zero_mul]

/-- Successive coefficientwise twists multiply their characters. -/
theorem dirichletCharacterTwist_comp {q : ℕ} (ψ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) :
    dirichletCharacterTwist ψ (dirichletCharacterTwist χ f) =
      dirichletCharacterTwist (ψ * χ) f := by
  ext n
  simp [MulChar.mul_apply, mul_assoc]

/-- Coefficientwise character twist is a homomorphism for Dirichlet convolution. -/
theorem dirichletCharacterTwist_mul {q : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (f g : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) :
    dirichletCharacterTwist χ (f * g) =
      dirichletCharacterTwist χ f * dirichletCharacterTwist χ g := by
  ext n
  simp only [dirichletCharacterTwist_apply, ArithmeticFunction.mul_apply, Finset.mul_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro x hx
  have hprod : x.1 * x.2 = n := (Nat.mem_divisorsAntidiagonal.mp hx).1
  rw [← hprod, Nat.cast_mul, map_mul]
  ring

/-- Inverse twisting is exactly level depletion, not identity in general. -/
theorem dirichletCharacterTwist_inv_twist {q : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) :
    dirichletCharacterTwist χ⁻¹ (dirichletCharacterTwist χ f) =
      characterLevelDepletion q f := by
  rw [dirichletCharacterTwist_comp, MulChar.inv_mul]
  rfl

end


end RHTower

/-!
# Diagonal curved families are flat after logarithmic differentiation

A homogeneous scalar twisted observable — one transformed in every source direction by
multiplication by a base element — has a logarithmic derivative which shifts *additively*, by the
logarithmic derivative of the twist.  Applied coordinatewise to a family whose adjoint local
system has been gauged to a diagonal one, this turns a curved datum into a flat one without any
cocycle equation: the boundary classes of the curved family are the classes of the logarithmic
derivatives of its twists.

The passage loses no differential rank, because an element and its logarithmic derivative are
mutually differentially algebraic.  So the whole flat source-boundary theory computes the rank of
a diagonalizable homogeneous curved family, with the logarithmic derivatives of the diagonal
twists as its boundary data.
-/

open Set
open scoped Differential

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

universe u

variable {C K L : Type u} [Field C] [Field K] [Field L]
  [Algebra C K] [Algebra C L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower C K L]
  [Differential K] [Differential L] [DifferentialAlgebra K L]
  {I : Type u} (tau : I → K ≃+* K) (sigma : I → L ≃+* L)

variable {κ : Type u} [Fintype κ]

/-- The logarithmic derivative of a family. -/
def logDerivFamily (y : κ → L) (p : κ) : L := (y p)′ / y p

/-- The logarithmic derivative of a family of twists. -/
def logDerivTwist (m : I → κ → K) (i : I) (p : κ) : K := (m i p)′ / m i p

/-! ### The curved scalar law becomes flat -/

omit [Fintype κ] in
/-- **A homogeneous diagonal curved family is flat after logarithmic differentiation.**  Its
increments are the logarithmic derivatives of the diagonal twists. -/
theorem logDerivFamily_shift {y : κ → L} {m : I → κ → K}
    (hderiv : ∀ i w, sigma i w′ = (sigma i w)′)
    (hy : ∀ p, y p ≠ 0) (hm : ∀ i p, m i p ≠ 0)
    (hmul : ∀ i p, sigma i (y p) = algebraMap K L (m i p) * y p) (i : I) (p : κ) :
    sigma i (logDerivFamily y p)
      = logDerivFamily y p + algebraMap K L (logDerivTwist m i p) :=
  GaloisForLFunctions.ringEquiv_deriv_div_self_of_mul (sigma i) (hderiv i) (y p) (m i p)
    (hy p) (hm i p) (hmul i p)

/-! ### The passage keeps the differential rank -/

omit [Fintype κ] in
theorem differentialClosure_logDerivFamily [CharZero L] (y : κ → L) :
    differentialClosure K (Set.range (logDerivFamily y))
      = differentialClosure K (Set.range y) := by
  have hlog : Set.range (logDerivFamily y) ⊆ differentialClosure K (Set.range y) := by
    rintro - ⟨p, rfl⟩
    have hmem := (GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.raw_logCoordinate_mutuallyDifferentialAlgebraic
      (F := K) (y p)).2
    exact GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.differentialAlgebraicOver_mono_differentialAdjoin
      (differentialAdjoin K (Set.range y)) (derivationClosed_differentialAdjoin K _)
      (by rintro - rfl; exact subset_differentialAdjoin K _ ⟨p, rfl⟩) hmem
  have hraw : Set.range y ⊆ differentialClosure K (Set.range (logDerivFamily y)) := by
    rintro - ⟨p, rfl⟩
    have hmem := (GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.raw_logCoordinate_mutuallyDifferentialAlgebraic
      (F := K) (y p)).1
    exact GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.differentialAlgebraicOver_mono_differentialAdjoin
      (differentialAdjoin K (Set.range (logDerivFamily y)))
      (derivationClosed_differentialAdjoin K _)
      (by rintro - rfl; exact subset_differentialAdjoin K _ ⟨p, rfl⟩) hmem
  refine subset_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · have := differentialClosure_mono (F := K) hlog
    rwa [differentialClosure_idempotent] at this
  · have := differentialClosure_mono (F := K) hraw
    rwa [differentialClosure_idempotent] at this

omit [Fintype κ] in
/-- The logarithmic derivative family has the same differential rank. -/
theorem eRk_logDerivFamily [CharZero L] (y : κ → L) :
    (differentialMatroid K L).eRk (Set.range (logDerivFamily y))

  rw [← Matroid.eRk_closure_eq, ← Matroid.eRk_closure_eq (X := Set.range y),

    differentialMatroid_closure_eq_differentialClosure,
    differentialClosure_logDerivFamily y]

/-!
# The first moment on an arbitrary interval

Translating the frequency of a Dirichlet polynomial twists its coefficients by unimodular factors, so the `ℓ²` mass
is unchanged and the large-values first-moment bound holds on *every* interval of a given length, not only on the
canonical one:

`∫_{t₀}^{t₀+2nΔ} ‖D(t)‖ dt ≤ 2Δ·√(n·((2n+1)Δ + 4N(1+log N))(1/Δ + 2 log N)·∑‖a_i‖²)`.

In particular it applies to `[−T, T]` with `t₀ = −T` and `2nΔ = 2T`, which is the range a Perron integral runs over.
-/

noncomputable section
namespace RHTower.Sieve
open Complex Finset

/-- **Translating the frequency of a Dirichlet polynomial twists its coefficients.**  The twist is unimodular, so
the `ℓ²` mass is unchanged. -/
theorem dirPoly_translate (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → ℂ) (t₀ t : ℝ) :
    dirPoly N a (t₀ + t)
      = dirPoly N (fun i => a i
          * Complex.exp (((t₀ * Real.log (((i : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) : ℝ) : ℂ) * I)) t := by
  rw [dirPoly, dirPoly]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
  rw [mul_assoc, ← Complex.exp_add]
  congr 1
  push_cast
  ring_nf

theorem norm_dirPoly_twist_coeff (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → ℂ) (t₀ : ℝ) (i : Fin N) :
    ‖a i * Complex.exp (((t₀ * Real.log (((i : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) : ℝ) : ℂ) * I)‖ = ‖a i‖ := by
  rw [norm_mul, Complex.norm_exp_ofReal_mul_I, mul_one]

/-- **The first moment on an arbitrary interval.**  The bound of the large-values composition holds on every
interval of the same length: translating the frequency twists the coefficients without changing their `ℓ²` mass. -/
theorem integral_norm_dirPoly_le_largeValues_shift (N : ℕ) (hN : 2 ≤ N) (a : Fin N → ℂ) {Δ : ℝ}
    (hΔ : 0 < Δ) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (t₀ : ℝ) :
    (∫ t in t₀..(t₀ + ((2 * n : ℕ) : ℝ) * Δ), ‖dirPoly N a t‖)
      ≤ 2 * Δ * Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ)
          * ((((2 * n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Δ + 4 * (N : ℝ) * (1 + Real.log N))
              * (1 / Δ + 2 * Real.log N) * ∑ i : Fin N, ‖a i‖ ^ 2)) := by
  classical
  set s : ℝ := t₀ - Δ / 2 with hs
  set ã : Fin N → ℂ := fun i => a i
    * Complex.exp (((s * Real.log (((i : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) : ℝ) : ℂ) * I) with hã
  have hmass : ∑ i : Fin N, ‖ã i‖ ^ 2 = ∑ i : Fin N, ‖a i‖ ^ 2 := by
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    rw [hã]
    simp only
    rw [norm_dirPoly_twist_coeff N a s i]
  have hshift : ∀ t : ℝ, ‖dirPoly N a (s + t)‖ = ‖dirPoly N ã t‖ := by
    intro t
    rw [dirPoly_translate N a s t]
  -- move the interval to the canonical position
  have hint : (∫ t in t₀..(t₀ + ((2 * n : ℕ) : ℝ) * Δ), ‖dirPoly N a t‖)
      = ∫ u in (Δ / 2)..(Δ / 2 + ((2 * n : ℕ) : ℝ) * Δ), ‖dirPoly N ã u‖ := by
    have hcomp := intervalIntegral.integral_comp_add_left
      (a := Δ / 2) (b := Δ / 2 + ((2 * n : ℕ) : ℝ) * Δ) (fun t => ‖dirPoly N a t‖) s
    rw [show s + Δ / 2 = t₀ by rw [hs]; ring,
      show s + (Δ / 2 + ((2 * n : ℕ) : ℝ) * Δ) = t₀ + ((2 * n : ℕ) : ℝ) * Δ by rw [hs]; ring] at hcomp
    rw [← hcomp]
    exact intervalIntegral.integral_congr (fun u _ => hshift u)
  rw [hint, ← hmass]
  exact integral_norm_dirPoly_le_largeValues N hN ã hΔ n hn

end RHTower.Sieve
